mfg1-surface-lesson-068.title: Compare paint classifications with appearance and durability requirements
mfg1-surface-lesson-068.objective:
Organize water/solvent media, resins and mixing formats separately.
Distinguish where to confirm electrocoat polarity and curing.
mfg1-surface-lesson-068.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 8 on four classifications, 8 distinguishing electrocoating and 7 organizing a similar-product change sheet. Write safety-information sources in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-068.summary:
Combine classifications to read product-specific conditions.
Same resin name, color or use of electricity does not mean interchangeability.
safety: Do not mix different paints or hardeners merely because their resin names match.
Do not change electrocoating polarity or connections for learning.

paragraphs.title: One label can contain several classifications
paragraphs.text: Paints can be classified by water-based or solvent-based medium, resin such as acrylic, urethane, silicone or fluororesin, and one- or two-component format. One classification does not determine all conditions. Check formulation, designated undercoat, drying and curing, and service environment together.

paragraphs.title: Confirm the electrocoating method
paragraphs.text: Electrocoating includes anionic and cationic methods, with different workpiece electrode roles and material conditions. Using electricity in both does not justify applying metal-plating polarity, equipment or bath conditions. The responsible person checks the designated supply and connections.

paragraphs.title: Do not rank durability by resin name alone
paragraphs.text: A resin described as highly durable in general examples does not unconditionally give the longest life in every environment. Do not infer that water-based means harmless or powder means no dust control. Read the SDS and product specification for required safety controls and evaluations.

paragraphs.title: Before substituting a similar product
paragraphs.text: For another product with the same resin name, compare base, hardener, ratio, usable time and curing conditions. Even the same color may require trials or first-piece checks. Follow change procedures and approvals.

terms.meaning: A paint category using water as the main medium.
A material involved in coating formation and related functions.
A format used as one paint component.
A format combining a specified base and hardener or similar components.

mfg1-surface-lesson-069.title: Read anodic-film structure and hard-anodizing conditions
mfg1-surface-lesson-069.objective:
Distinguish barrier and porous layers.
Check relationships among supply type, coloring, sealing and performance.
mfg1-surface-lesson-069.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 8 on film structure, 8 on coloring and supplies and 7 organizing hard-coating requirements. Check representative-value limits in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-069.summary:
Match structure, supply, coloring and sealing to specifications.
Evaluate hard-film properties using conditions and tests too.
safety: Do not set bath recipes, temperatures or supply modes from learning material.
Do not use withstand-voltage examples as guarantees of human-protection insulation.

paragraphs.title: The film grows from the substrate
paragraphs.text: In aluminium anodizing the workpiece is on the anode side, and part of its surface becomes oxide to form a film. Do not equate the thin natural oxide with a controlled-process film's thickness. Film thickness and substrate consumption are not simply identical; check process and material conditions.

paragraphs.title: Pores and the barrier layer
paragraphs.text: A typical porous film contains a porous portion and a dense barrier layer next to the substrate. Dye coloring, coloration related to material constituents or electrolysis conditions, and secondary electrolytic coloring have different mechanisms. Some methods use AC or superimposed supplies as well as DC; names alone do not determine settings.

paragraphs.title: Tradeoffs in hard films and post-treatment
paragraphs.text: Hard anodizing targets wear resistance and similar properties, but temperature, thickness and sealing depend on required-performance tradeoffs. Do not assume that every hard coating must remain unsealed or that thicker always gives the best insulation. Confirm through specifications and designated tests.

paragraphs.title: Treat heat and electrical values as representative
paragraphs.text: Do not turn representative heat-resistance temperatures or withstand voltages into actual part heating limits or guarantees of shock protection. The responsible person evaluates shape, defects, dyes, thermal-expansion differences and service environment. Do not improvise electrical or high-temperature tests.

terms.meaning: The dense oxide layer next to the substrate.
The portion of a coating containing fine pores.

terms.reading: こうしつようきょくさんか
terms.meaning: An anodizing category targeting high hardness, wear resistance and related properties.

mfg1-surface-lesson-070.title: Check abrasive particles and supply formats by product
mfg1-surface-lesson-070.objective:
Identify alumina, silica, chromium oxide and similar particles.
Manage solid, liquid and particle-containing buffs separately.
mfg1-surface-lesson-070.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 8 on particles and names, 8 on supply formats and 7 organizing substitution checks. Explain contamination and cleaning in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-070.summary:
Check item number, particles and use rather than color or nickname.
Manage buffs, compounds and supply methods separately.
safety: Do not improvise manual supply or cleaning while equipment rotates.
Do not mix unknown compounds or directly inhale their dust.

paragraphs.title: Names and composition are different
paragraphs.text: Compounds use particles such as alumina, silica and chromium oxide. Names such as Saizer, lime, red bar, white bar and green bar help select products, but color or trade names alone do not establish every product's composition and fineness. Compare label, item number and specified use.

paragraphs.title: Separate coarse removal and finishing
paragraphs.text: Coarse polishing removes large scratches and burrs; finishing reduces fine scratches to the required appearance. General examples use red, white and green bars at different stages, but there is no fixed sequence for every case. Check substrate, required appearance and buff combination against approved specifications.

paragraphs.title: Check supply and cleaning conditions
paragraphs.text: Solid compounds bind particles into a solid form; liquid compounds disperse particles in liquid. For liquids, manage spray, contamination and supply method; for solids, application amount and condition. Some nonwoven buffs contain particles. Even soft material can scratch if coarse particles or foreign matter are present.

paragraphs.title: Prevent carrying in a different material
paragraphs.text: If finishing compound runs short, do not replenish with a similarly colored product. Compare item number, particles, buff, work material and cleaning method, and hold unconfirmed items. When changing supply amounts or methods, follow procedures addressing spray, dust and entanglement.

terms.meaning: Aluminium oxide, a material used for abrasive particles.
Silicon oxide, a material used for abrasive particles.
A chromium oxide used for abrasive particles and related applications.

terms.reading: えきじょうけんまざい
terms.meaning: A compound with abrasive particles dispersed in liquid.

mfg1-surface-lesson-071.title: Understand safety-and-health responsibilities and greetings
mfg1-surface-lesson-071.objective:
Explain the Industrial Safety and Health Act's purpose and three pillars.
Distinguish specialist contacts from everyday greetings.
mfg1-surface-lesson-071.activity: Spend 6 minutes organizing the three pillars, 8 on roles and establishment conditions, 8 distinguishing greetings from specific hazard reports and 5 explaining how to find contacts. Summarize emergency differences in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-071.summary:
Connect standards, responsibilities and voluntary activities.
Check workplace contacts and distinguish greetings from specific reports.
safety: Do not delay urgent danger or health responses until a committee meeting or routine consultation.
Do not replace hazard reports or necessary work checks with greetings.

paragraphs.title: A framework for protecting safety and health
paragraphs.text:
The Industrial Safety and Health Act is Japanese law protecting workers' safety and health. The text organizes it into establishing hazard-prevention standards, clarifying responsibilities and promoting voluntary activities. Companies and workers follow the standards and procedures applicable to them.
Voluntary activity does not mean freely omitting laws or safety devices. It means identifying workplace hazards, discussing measures and continuing approved activities.

paragraphs.title: Check roles and consultation contacts
paragraphs.text:
Safety and health committees and similar bodies discuss safety and health issues. Safety managers handle safety-related management, while occupational physicians contribute specialist expertise to worker health management and related matters.
Appointment or establishment duties and roles vary with industry, establishment size and other conditions. Do not assume every factory needs identical organizations or staffing; check your workplace structure and contacts. Do not wait for a committee meeting during an abnormality: follow emergency communication, stopping and evacuation procedures.
Ask the responsible person about the subjects and timing of special health examinations associated with harmful work and similar conditions. Receive designated examinations and follow health management. Examinations do not replace exposure prevention such as ventilation.

paragraphs.title: Use greetings as a starting point for communication
paragraphs.text:
Greet people you pass with situation-appropriate expressions such as good morning, thank you for your work or work safely. Speaking with people in different occupations helps you know one another and makes consultation and communication easier.
A greeting alone does not communicate a hazard or work instruction. Report the location, condition and required response specifically when you notice an abnormality. Do not enter hazardous areas to greet someone or carelessly distract a person operating equipment.

paragraphs.title: When you do not know the health contact
paragraphs.text: Suppose you wish to discuss how you feel after work but do not know the contact. Use the workplace contact list or supervisor to check health-consultation services and occupational-physician arrangements. Do not assume another factory's arrangements apply. For sudden danger or health abnormalities, request help through emergency procedures without waiting for a routine appointment.

terms.meaning: A system clarifying who holds each role and responsibility.

terms.reading: あんぜんえいせいいいんかい
terms.meaning: A body discussing safety and health issues; check applicable rules for establishment conditions.
A physician contributing specialist expertise to worker health management and related matters.
Everyday communication that also helps build relationships in which contact is easier.
